$comment: Content layer. Extracted verbatim from the P0/P1 prototype data (measured from the source playbook). No styling here.
summary: A starting shape, four rules and a job for every position.
gives: four players who can quickly join an attack
shapeCue: The formation is our starting position. It isn't where we have to stand.

shape.title: Starting shape: 1-3-1-3-1
shape.caption: The formation is our starting position. It isn't where we have to stand.
shape.altSummary: Nine players attacking upwards in a 1-3-1-3-1: goalkeeper; 3, 5 and 2 across the back; 6 alone in front of them; 11, 10 and 7 across the middle with 10 central; 9 furthest forward. A shaded spine runs through GK, 5, 6, 10 and 9.

rules.title: Middle first
rules.tag: Make it difficult for teams to play through us.
rules.summary: Protect the middle before chasing the ball outside.
rules.cue: If you're not sure whether to go, stay central.
rules.extra: We defend from inside to outside.
look: The 6 stays central, between the ball and our goal.
Nobody leaves a gap in front of the centre-back (5) to chase the ball wide.

rules.title: One goes, one stays
rules.tag: We can attack without leaving ourselves wide open.
rules.summary: One outside defender can attack. The other stays.
rules.cue: If the other defender goes, you stay.
rules.extra: Staying means moving inside a little, next to 5.
rules.seo: One goes, one stays: outside defenders in 9v9
look: Ball on the right: 2 goes; 3, 5 and 6 protect us.
Ball on the left: 3 goes; 2, 5 and 6 protect us.
Never both: if both go forward, both sides are open.

rules.title: Far side in
rules.tag: Don't watch the attack. Join it.
rules.summary: When we attack down one side, the opposite wide player attacks the goal.
rules.cue: Ball on your side: give us width. Ball on the other side: attack the goal.
rules.extra: Not one striker: three players who can score.
rules.seo: Far side in: attacking the far post in 9v9
look: 7 has the ball. 9 keeps their defenders busy. 10 supports. 11 gets in at the far post.
Down the left it mirrors: 11 has the ball and 7 gets in at the far post.

rules.title: Show them wide, then go
rules.tag: We don't need to chase the ball everywhere.
rules.summary: Protect the middle, guide them to the touchline, then press together.
rules.extra: Go means the nearest players press together. It doesn't mean everyone charges at the ball.
rules.seo: Show them wide, then go: pressing in 9v9
look: Show them wide: 9 curves the run. The pass across or through the middle gets hard; the pass wide looks easy.
Go: 7 presses, 10 blocks the pass inside, 9 blocks the pass back, 6 protects behind. Everyone shifts across.

roles.title: Goalkeeper
roles.head: Start us playing
points: With the ball: short to 3, 5 or 2. The 6 is available in the middle, just ahead.
Without it: talk. Left. Right. Man on. Turn. Drop.
roles.cue: Look short first. If it isn't on, don't force it.

roles.title: Centre-back
roles.head: Keep us secure
points: Protect the middle.
Don't get dragged out unless somebody covers you.
If nobody presses you, carry the ball forward.
steps: Sooner or later an opponent has to come to you.
Now a teammate is free. Pass.

roles.title: Outside defenders
roles.head: Defend first. Support second.
points: Your jobs, in order: defend, help us build, join the attack.
Ball right: 2 can go forward. 3 tucks in, almost another centre-back.
Ball left: 3 can go forward. 2 tucks in, almost another centre-back.

roles.title: The screen
roles.head: Protect. Connect.
points: Stay underneath the ball. Stay central.
Show for possession. Protect us when we lose it.
situations: Get between the attacker and 5. Slow them down, so teammates recover and we defend together.
Move to find an angle. Then ask: can I turn? Yes: look forward. No: play safely and move again.
roles.cue: You don't have to win every tackle. Sometimes stopping them going forward is enough.

roles.title: Wide players
roles.head: Wide when it's ours. Narrow when it isn't.
points: Ball on your side: move wide. Give the player on the ball an easy pass.
Ball on the other side: move inside. Attack the goal.
They have the ball: recover towards the centre first. Help protect the middle, in a line with the 6.
roles.cue: Where's the ball? That tells you where to go.

roles.title: Number 10
roles.head: Find the space
points: Find pockets of space.
Get close enough to support 9.
Look forward when you receive.
Help us press when we lose it.
You're not just a dribbler. You connect midfield and attack.
situations: Stay close to 9 so you can press together. Don't drop all the way back next to 6.
roles.cue: Can I receive facing their goal?

roles.title: Striker
roles.head: Give us somewhere to play
points: Stretch the defence.
Give us a forward pass.
Protect the ball when needed.
Start our press.
Know when to come short and when to run behind.
situations: 9 threatens the space behind. Their defenders drop, and space opens for 10.
9 checks towards the ball. A defender follows, and space opens behind.
roles.cue: Both moves make space for teammates.

roles.title: 9 and 10 together
roles.head: Don't stand in a line
points: Too easy: 9 and 10 in the same line are easy to mark, and the pass to either is blocked.
9 runs, 10 receives: 9 stretches, 10 finds space.
9 comes, 10 goes: one comes, one goes.

frames.caption: 6 is dragged to the touchline. A big gap opens in front of 5.
frames.altSummary: An opponent on our right has the ball. Our 6 has run from the centre towards them, leaving a grey gap in front of the centre-back, and the opponent passes into it.

frames.caption: 6 stays central, between the ball and our goal. The middle is closed.
frames.altSummary: The same opponent has the ball on our right. Our 6 stays in the centre inside a shaded key space, so the pass into the middle is blocked, shown by a cross.

frames.caption: 2 goes. 3, 5 and 6 protect us.
frames.altSummary: Our 7 has the ball on the right. Our 2 runs forward to support. 3 tucks in towards 5, and 3, 5 and 6 form a shaded protective block in the middle.

frames.caption: 3 goes. 2, 5 and 6 protect us.
frames.altSummary: Mirror image. Our 11 has the ball on the left. Our 3 runs forward. 2 tucks in towards 5, and 2, 5 and 6 protect the middle.

frames.caption: Both go forward: both sides are open.
frames.altSummary: Our 7 has the ball. Both outside defenders, 2 and 3, have run forward, leaving two grey open spaces either side of 5 near our penalty area.

frames.caption: 7 has the ball. 9 keeps their defenders busy. 10 supports. 11 gets in at the far post.
frames.altSummary: We attack down the right. 7 has the ball wide; 10 offers a short pass inside; 9 occupies the defenders; 11 runs from the far side to the far post, where a curved cross from 7 arrives in a shaded key space.

frames.caption: 11 has the ball. 7 gets in at the far post. Not one striker: three players who can score.
frames.altSummary: Mirror image. We attack down the left: 11 has the ball, 10 supports, 9 occupies defenders, and 7 runs from the far side to the far post.

frames.caption: 9 curves the run. The pass across or through the middle gets hard. The pass wide looks easy.
frames.altSummary: An opponent defender has the ball. Our 9 steps across from in front of another opponent to block the pass across the pitch, shown by a cross, so the easy pass is out wide into a shaded key space by the touchline. 10, 11, 7 and 6 hold their positions behind.

frames.caption: 7 presses. 10 blocks the pass inside. 9 blocks the pass back. 6 protects behind. Everyone shifts across.
frames.altSummary: The opponent now has the ball near the right touchline. Our 7 runs up to press. 10 steps across to block the pass inside, shown by a cross. 9 runs across past the opponent centre-back to block the pass back. 11 and 6 shift across behind.
frames.note: The curve of 9's run is approximate; the source arrow bows around the opponent.

frames.caption: 9 and 10 in the same line. They are easy to mark, and the pass to either is blocked.
frames.altSummary: Our 6 has the ball near halfway. 9 and 10 stand one behind the other in the middle, surrounded by six opponents, inside a grey box.

frames.caption: 9 stretches. 10 finds space.
frames.altSummary: 9 runs in behind towards goal, pulling defenders back. 10 receives a pass from 6 in the shaded space that opens between the lines.

frames.caption: One comes. One goes.
frames.altSummary: 9 drops short towards 6 to receive, and 10 runs past 9 into the space behind towards goal.

frames.caption: Short to 3, 5 or 2. 6 is available in the middle, just ahead.
frames.altSummary: Our goalkeeper has the ball. Dashed passes go short to 3, 5 and 2. The 6 stands in a shaded circle just ahead, between three opponents.

frames.caption: 1 Carry: space ahead, so 5 carries it forward. 2 They come: an opponent has to come to 5. 3 Pass: now a teammate is free.
frames.altSummary: Our 5 carries the ball forward from the back. An opponent steps up to close them down, so 5 passes to the 10, who is now free on the left of midfield.
frames.note: The opponent's arrow is shorter in the source; its start point here is approximate.

frames.caption: 2 can go forward. 3 tucks in, almost another centre-back.
frames.altSummary: Our 7 has the ball on the right. 2 goes forward to support. 3 tucks in next to 5. 6 stays in front.

frames.caption: 3 can go forward. 2 tucks in, almost another centre-back.
frames.altSummary: Mirror image. Our 11 has the ball on the left. 3 goes forward. 2 tucks in next to 5.

frames.caption: Get between the attacker and 5. Slow them down, teammates recover, we defend together.
frames.altSummary: An opponent with the ball runs at us through the middle. Our 6 stays in a shaded circle between the attacker and 5, while 11 and 7 recover inside from wide.

frames.caption: Move to find an angle, then ask: can I turn? Yes: look forward. No: play safely and move again.
frames.altSummary: Our 5 has won the ball. The 6 moves to an angle and receives. Two dashed options follow: forward to 10, marked yes, or back out to 3, marked no.

frames.caption: Move wide. Give the player on the ball an easy pass.
frames.altSummary: Our 2 has the ball on the right. 7 moves out wide to the touchline and receives a pass from 2.

frames.caption: Move inside. Attack the goal. Far side in.
frames.altSummary: Our 3 has the ball on the left and passes to 11. On the far side, 7 runs inside from the right touchline towards goal, near 9.

frames.caption: Recover towards the centre first. Help protect the middle.
frames.altSummary: Opponents have the ball in midfield. 11 and 7 recover inside to form a line with 6 in a shaded band, labelled 11, 6, 7, in front of the back three.

frames.caption: Find pockets of space between their lines. Get close enough to support 9.
frames.altSummary: Our 6 passes forward to 10, who has found space in a wide shaded band between two lines of three opponents, close to 9.

frames.caption: Stay close to 9 so you can press together. Don't drop all the way back next to 6.
frames.altSummary: Opponents have the ball near their goal. 9 and 10 stay close together in a shaded box to press. A cross next to 6, labelled not here, shows where 10 should not drop to.

frames.caption: 9 threatens the space behind. Their defenders drop, and space opens for 10.
frames.altSummary: 9 runs from the edge of the shaded space in behind the defence, and 10 has the ball in the space that opens behind 9, with a dashed pass option to 9.
frames.note: Running behind involves offside at 9v9. Our offside guidance is awaiting review.

frames.caption: 9 checks towards the ball. A defender follows, and space opens behind.
frames.altSummary: 9 drops towards 6 to receive. An opponent defender follows 9, leaving a shaded space behind near their goal. 10 is wide on the right.

review.title: Offside, and how to introduce it
review.why: Offside starts at 9v9 and the source playbook does not cover it.
qs: How should a coach first explain offside to players new to it?
Which of our pictures depend on it (the striker running behind, pressing high)?
What should players be told about staying onside when the far-side player attacks the goal?

review.title: Strengths and weaknesses of 1-3-1-3-1
review.why: The source lists what the shape gives us, not what it costs.
qs: Where is this shape most exposed?
Which player profiles make it easier or harder to play?
When might a coach choose a different 9v9 shape?

review.title: When opponents play three forwards
review.why: With three at the back and one outside defender going forward, numbers can be level at the back.
qs: Does one goes, one stays still hold, or should both stay?
Is this worth covering for this age group at all?

review.title: Developing players across roles
review.why: England Football encourages letting players try different positions. How to do that with this shape is not written.
qs: How often should players change role?
Which roles pair well for learning?
How do we keep the four rules while players rotate?
